پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «پریکاردیت کنستریکتیو» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

ارزیابی تحلیلی گزینه‌های دیگر: سایر گزینه‌ها به دلیل اثربخشی کمتر، تطابق ناکافی با معیارهای قطعی راهنماهای بالینی، یا داشتن عوارض جانبی و تأخیر در روند بهبودی در مقایسه با «پریکاردیت کنستریکتیو» در اولویت بعدی قرار گرفته و رد می‌شوند.
questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.question_en: A 75-year-old man presented with sudden RUQ pain, chills, and jaundice. In the examination, he has a fever of 40 degrees and BP=120/80 mmHg. In CBC, leukocytosis was 20,000 and in ultrasound, numerous stones in the gallbladder were reported. Which action is correct after starting antibiotics?

پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «ERCP و اسفنکتروتومی» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

ارزیابی تحلیلی گزینه‌های دیگر: سایر گزینه‌ها به دلیل اثربخشی کمتر، تطابق ناکافی با معیارهای قطعی راهنماهای بالینی، یا داشتن عوارض جانبی و تأخیر در روند بهبودی در مقایسه با «ERCP و اسفنکتروتومی» در اولویت بعدی قرار گرفته و رد می‌شوند.
questions.explanation_en: Pruritus, direct hyperbilirubinemia and high ALP/GGT with ultrasound ducts suggest normal intrahepatic cholestasis. Most middle-aged women have PBC, AMA positive and small intrahepatic duct destruction; With cholestatic enzymes and AMA, biopsy is usually not required for diagnosis unless there is overlap/uncertainty. PSC is more male and UC, multifocal intra/extrahepatic strictures on MRCP and risk of cholangiocarcinoma. Gallbladder stone without duct dilation is usually incidental. ERCP for obstruction/therapeutic intervention, not first-line diagnosis in uncomplicated PBC/PSC.

questions.explanation_en: Pruritus, direct hyperbilirubinemia and high ALP/GGT with ultrasound ducts suggest normal intrahepatic cholestasis. Most middle-aged women have PBC, AMA positive and small intrahepatic duct destruction; With cholestatic enzymes and AMA, biopsy is usually not required for diagnosis unless there is overlap/uncertainty. PSC is more male and UC, multifocal intra/extrahepatic strictures on MRCP and risk of cholangiocarcinoma. Gallbladder stone without duct dilation is usually incidental. ERCP for obstruction/therapeutic intervention, not first-line diagnosis in uncomplicated PBC/PSC.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: Chronic pancreatitis, especially with alcohol, causes pancreatic exocrine insufficiency, smelly/bulky steatorrhea, weight loss, and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency. Fecal elastase is a non-invasive test and secretin stimulation is more sensitive but invasive/hardly available. Treatment is alcohol/smoking cessation, pancreatic enzymes along with food and nutrition. High pleural fluid amylase is seen in pancreatitis/pseudocyst, esophageal rupture and some malignancies, and TB is less important. Acute pancreatitis with early enteral feeding, analgesia and fluid goal-directed management and antibiotic prophylaxis is not routine.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: Asymptomatic gallstones usually require observation, and prophylactic cholecystectomy is considered only in selected conditions such as porcelain gallbladder, large polyp, hemolytic anemia, or specific transplant/high-risk. Obesity, rapid weight loss, female sex and cirrhosis increase the risk of stones. Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: Dysphagia solids then progressive liquids are more mechanical cancer/stricture and solids+liquids are more motility like achalasia from the beginning. High age, rapid course and weight loss suggest pseudoachalasia/malignancy and make upper endoscopy necessary. achalasia is helped by confirmatory manometry and bird-beak barium swallow; POEM treatment is pneumatic dilation or Heller myotomy. Absent barium imaging should be reported explicitly. Ring only gives intermittent solid dysphagia and diffuse spasm simultaneous dysphagia/chest pain with corkscrew.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: Average-risk CRC screening starts at the age of 45. In first-degree relative with CRC or advanced adenoma before age 60, colonoscopy is recommended starting at age 40 or 10 years earlier than family diagnosis—whichever is earlier—and every 5 years. If the mother is infected at the age of 26, hereditary syndrome such as Lynch/FAP should be investigated with genetic counseling and the usual options may not be correct. questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. Antibiotic prophylaxis is prohibited in sterile necrosis. infected necrosis is managed with antibiotic penetrating necrosis and step-up approach including drainage and delayed minimally invasive necrosectomy; Immediate open surgery is usually not preferred. questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. questions.explanation_en: Irritable bowel syndrome is defined by recurrent abdominal pain associated with defecation and change in stool frequency or shape, without explanatory structural damage. Warning signs include onset at an advanced age, weight loss, blood, anemia, fever, nocturnal diarrhea, family history of IBD/cancer, and elevated inflammatory markers and require organic investigation. Treatment is with education, soluble fiber such as psyllium, short-term guided low-FODMAP diet, antispasmodic, and subtype therapy; Rifaximin for IBS-D and low-dose TCA are useful in selected pain/IBS-D. options_why_fa: نادرست است؛ دلیل رد: «آندوسکوپی» در مقایسه با پاسخ صحیح و شرایط بالینی بیمار در هاریسون، اقدام اولویت‌دار یا انتخاب اول بالینی محسوب نمی‌شود.

questions.explanation_fa:
تحلیل بالینی و صورت مسئله: در این سناریو، بیمار با تظاهرات «آقای 48 سالهای با هماتوشزی مراجعه نموده است. علائم حیاتی، Stable است و Tilt منفی است. اقدام بعدی کدام است؟» در حیطه تخصصی گوارش تحت ارزیابی قرار گرفته است. با استناد به مبانی تشخیصی و تصمیم‌گیری بالینی مرجع کانونی اصول طب داخلی هاریسون (ویرایش ۲۲)، بخش اختلالات دستگاه گوارش و کبد و پانکراس، اقدام انتخابی و پاسخ صحیح بالینی «کلونوسکوپی» می‌باشد.

پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «کلونوسکوپی» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

ارزیابی تحلیلی گزینه‌های دیگر: سایر گزینه‌ها به دلیل اثربخشی کمتر، تطابق ناکافی با معیارهای قطعی راهنماهای بالینی، یا داشتن عوارض جانبی و تأخیر در روند بهبودی در مقایسه با «کلونوسکوپی» در اولویت بعدی قرار گرفته و رد می‌شوند.
questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: Dysphagia solids then progressive liquids are more mechanical cancer/stricture and solids+liquids are more motility like achalasia from the beginning. questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

questions.explanation_en: Asymptomatic gallstones usually require observation, and prophylactic cholecystectomy is considered only in selected conditions such as porcelain gallbladder, large polyp, hemolytic anemia, or specific transplant/high-risk. Obesity, rapid weight loss, female sex and cirrhosis increase the risk of stones. Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

questions.explanation_en: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed with epigastric pain radiating to back and lipase/amylase more than three times or imaging. The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. Antibiotic prophylaxis is prohibited in sterile necrosis. infected necrosis is managed with antibiotic penetrating necrosis and step-up approach including drainage and delayed minimally invasive necrosectomy; Immediate open surgery is usually not preferred. In mild biliary pancreatitis, cholecystectomy reduces same admission recurrence and ERCP requires only cholangitis/ongoing obstruction.

questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

questions.explanation_en: Asymptomatic gallstones usually require observation, and prophylactic cholecystectomy is considered only in selected conditions such as porcelain gallbladder, large polyp, hemolytic anemia, or specific transplant/high-risk. Obesity, rapid weight loss, female sex and cirrhosis increase the risk of stones. Acute cholecystitis with RUQ pain, fever, Murphy and wall thickening/stones requires early laparoscopic cholecystectomy treatment. Renal failure is not the only indication for prophylactic surgery. UDCA is selected for small cholesterol stones in non-surgical patients with high recurrence.

questions.explanation_en: SAAG = serum albumin − ascitic albumin; A value of ≥1.1 indicates portal hypertension. High protein ascites with high SAAG leads to cardiac ascites, Budd-Chiari or early sinusoidal disease, and low protein leads to cirrhosis. SBP is diagnosed with PMN≥250/mm³ and treated immediately with cefotaxime/ceftriaxone; Bedside culture is taken before antibiotic. IV albumin in SBP with renal dysfunction/high bilirubin reduces the risk of HRS, but criteria are needed. Routine endoscopy is not an immediate action for an SBP episode unless there is a separate bleeding/screening indication.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

Warning signs include onset at an advanced age, weight loss, blood, anemia, fever, nocturnal diarrhea, family history of IBD/cancer, and elevated inflammatory markers and require organic investigation. Treatment is with education, soluble fiber such as psyllium, short-term guided low-FODMAP diet, antispasmodic, and subtype therapy; Rifaximin for IBS-D and low-dose TCA are useful in selected pain/IBS-D. questions.explanation_en: H. pylori is detected by urea breath test or active stool antigen and its eradication is confirmed by non-serological test at least four weeks after antibiotic and two weeks after stopping PPI. IgG remains positive for months/years after treatment and is not a test-of-cure. The choice of regimen depends on clarithromycin resistance and previous exposure; bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empirical choice in many areas. gastric ulcer should have endoscopy and biopsy from the edge to rule out malignancy and follow-up healing; Simple duodenal ulcer is more benign. Visible vessel bleeding ulcer requires endoscopic treatment and high-dose IV PPI.

questions.explanation_en: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed with epigastric pain radiating to back and lipase/amylase more than three times or imaging. The primary treatment is goal-directed lactated Ringer, analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding; A fixed volume of 5-6 liters is dangerous for everyone. Antibiotic prophylaxis is prohibited in sterile necrosis. infected necrosis is managed with antibiotic penetrating necrosis and step-up approach including drainage and delayed minimally invasive necrosectomy; Immediate open surgery is usually not preferred. In mild biliary pancreatitis, cholecystectomy reduces same admission recurrence and ERCP requires only cholangitis/ongoing obstruction.

questions.explanation_en: In acute HBV, HBsAg and anti-HBc IgM are positive and anti-HBs is negative; HBeAg shows proliferation but may be negative in precore mutant. The window period is known only with anti-HBc IgM and isolated anti-HBs after vaccination. Acute hepatitis B is often treated in supportive adults; Antiviral is selected for acute liver failure or severe/protracted disease. PT/INR, mental status, glucose and bilirubin determine the severity. HBV DNA is important for baseline/chronic disease management, not a requirement for acute serological diagnosis in all patients.

پاتوفیزیولوژی و استدلال گایدلاین هاریسون: انتخاب «به بیمار اطمینان داده شود که بیماری کلیوی ندارد (پروتئینوری ارتوستاتیک خوش‌خیم)» بر اساس رویکرد گام‌به‌گام طب مبتنی بر شواهد استوار است. این استراتژی درمانی/تشخیصی با هدف تثبیت وضعیت همودینامیک، مهار فرآیندهای پاتولوژیک زمینه‌ای و کاهش مورتالیتی و موربیدیتی ناشی از بیماری اتخاذ می‌گردد. در مدیریت بالینی این بیماری، توازن دقیق میان منافع مداخله و خطرات عوارض جانبی مطابق سرفصل‌های به‌روزشده هاریسون برقرار شده است.

questions.question_en: A 56-year-old woman presented with oliguria and limb edema. He has a history of high blood pressure, which is being treated with hydrochlorothiazide, and because of osteoarthritis, he has been taking ibuprofen for 6 months. He has a mild fever and macular erythematosus skin lesions are seen on the skin of the trunk and limbs. WBC=11000, EOS=12%, BUN=50 Urine protein=8 gr/24h, Cr=3, K=5 U/ A= (WBC=8-10, RBC=10-12, Prot=3+) Which of the following is the most likely cause of the patient's kidney failure?

questions.explanation_en: In GI bleeding, first ABC, two IV, type/cross, CBC/coag and resuscitation are performed; Endoscopy is not performed before hemodynamic stabilization. Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. In persistent lower bleeding, colonoscopy after bowel prep; In ongoing brisk bleed, CT angiography and then embolization is useful. A visible hemorrhoid in a person over 45 or with anemia/change bowel habit does not rule out cancer and colonoscopy is necessary. NSAID raises bleeding risk and melena upper source.

Hematochezia with shock and very high BUN/Cr can be upper GI brisk bleeding, and upper endoscopy is the priority after stabilization. Treatment is with education, soluble fiber such as psyllium, short-term guided low-FODMAP diet, antispasmodic, and subtype therapy; Rifaximin for IBS-D and low-dose TCA are useful in selected pain/IBS-D.
